messages.subject: Re: how to interpret co-variances ( ~~) in the model (SEM)?
parts:
If you allow covariance involving a dependent variable (such as an item loading on a common factor), this is residual covariance--covariance beyond what is expleined by the dependency relationship. In a factor model, items that load on common factors covary because of their joint dependency on the same common factor, or their dependency on different common factors that themselves covary. However in your base common factor model, these items are conditionally independent, conditioning on the common factors. With the addition of residual covariance, this is no longer true.

On Sun, Aug 12, 2018 at 11:56 PM Hyojung Lim <hyojung...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello, I'm non-statistician, very new to SEM. Sorry, if this is a silly question. 

I ran SEM like below. 

data <- read.csv("C:/sem/highschool.csv")
summary(data)
highschool.model <- 'ought =~ X10 + X18 + X26 + X41 + X48
ideal =~ X1 + X9 + X17 + X33 + X40
experience =~ X11 + X19 + X27 + X42
effort =~ X4 + X12 + X28 + X35 + X43
effort ~ ideal+ ought + experience'
highschool.fit <- sem (model = highschool.model, data = data)
summary(highschool.fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
modificationindices(highschool.fit, sort = TRUE)

As the modification indices suggest, I incorporated some ~~ into the model (see below) and thus CFI and TLI improved. 

data <- read.csv("C:/sem/highschool.csv")
summary(data)
highschool.model <- 'ideal =~ X1 + X9 + X17 + X33 + X40
ought =~ X10 + X18 + X26 + X41 + X48
experience =~ X11 + X19 + X27 + X34 + X42
effort =~ X4 + X12 + X20 + X28 + X35 + X43
effort ~ ideal + ought + experience
X34~~X28
X27~~X34
X1~~X9
X19~~X20'
highschool.fit <- sem (model = highschool.model, data = data)
summary(highschool.fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)


My question is "how to interpret" the revised model??

Does that just indicate a different assumption? The revised model assumes that those question items (X1, 9, 27, 34, 28, 19, 20) co-vary, while in the original model, every item is independent and loaded onto the relevant factor only?? Am I correct?
